About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey
column2:
every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

As a Product Manager - Integration, you’ll bring hands-on accounting expertise into a product environment to shape integrations that match real finance workflows. You’ll sit in our Accounting Integrations team and help ensure spend data (expenses, receipts, VAT, categories) flows cleanly from Pleo into the accounting systems and ERPs finance teams rely on, with minimal manual work. This is a hybrid role at the intersection of accounting domain knowledge, product thinking and technical partner collaboration, where your judgement will directly influence what we build and how it lands for customers.

You’ll own a portfolio of integrations and partners, turning customer needs and operational edge cases into clear requirements and improvements delivered with internal teams and external developers. Success in this role shows up in higher export success rates, fewer configuration-related issues and integrations that finance teams can trust at month-end.

Who you'll be working with and reporting to

You’ll be part of the Accounting Integrations team, focused on connecting Pleo with the accounting systems and ERPs most used by European finance teams.
You will report to our Group Product Manager from Integrations and will work closely with Product and Engineering to define requirements, make sound accounting decisions and support delivery across many different systems and data models.
You’ll also collaborate with external development partners and ERP vendors building on Pleo’s APIs, acting as a key point of contact to keep implementations on track and aligned with customer workflows.

What you'll be doing

As an Product Manager you will:

  • Own a portfolio of accounting integrations and partner relationships, balancing customer needs, partner requests and internal priorities.

  • Translate export, reconciliation and month-end close workflows into clear product requirements and integration behaviours.

  • Partner with engineers to define data mapping and implementation details across multiple accounting systems, data models and APIs.

  • Improve the integration set-up and configuration experience so customers can onboard successfully with fewer issues.

  • Act as a trusted accounting domain expert, making pragmatic decisions that improve data quality and reduce manual work for finance teams.

  • Support external partners and ERP vendors building on Pleo’s APIs, ensuring alignment on expectations, delivery and quality.

  • Track and improve outcomes such as export success rate, adoption/activation and integration-related support volume.

What you bring

Must have

  • Practical bookkeeping and finance process knowledge (expense coding, reconciliation and month-end close).

  • Strong understanding of how accountants, bookkeepers and finance leads work day to day.

  • A solid track record working with product teams from defining requirements through to delivery.

  • Experience managing external partners or senior stakeholders and delivering through influence.

  • Hands-on exposure to technology in a finance context (for example configuring accounting/ERP tools, working with integrations/data imports, or collaborating closely with technical teams).

Nice to have

  • Experience with European accounting and ERP systems, and/or an accounting qualification.

  • Partner negotiation experience and/or additional European languages.

  • Working knowledge of APIs, data mapping or implementation projects.

Why this role is a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You enjoy bringing real accounting expertise into product decisions and can explain complex finance concepts in a clear, practical way.

  • You like owning problems end to end - from identifying the right solution to working with others to ship it.

  • You’re motivated by improving workflows for finance teams and can connect day-to-day pain points to measurable outcomes.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

  • You want a role where you control delivery directly, rather than delivering through internal teams and external partners.

  • You prefer depth in a single system over context switching across many tools, markets and accounting practices.

  • You’re looking for a purely accounting or purely technical role, without the “bridge” work in between.

How you'll develop in this role

Within your first 6 months, you’ll build a deep understanding of customer export and reconciliation needs and how Pleo’s integrations behave in practice, then take ownership of a defined portfolio of integrations and partners. You’ll identify the highest-impact improvements to the integration set-up experience and drive them to delivery with internal teams.


Within 12 months, you’ll be a go-to expert for integration and accounting decisions, with measurable improvements in export success rates and a reduction in configuration-related issues. You’ll help launch new or improved integrations by enabling internal teams and partners with the context and clarity they need to deliver well.

Over time, you’ll strengthen your product toolkit (requirements, trade-offs, delivery rituals) and build deeper technical fluency by working side-by-side with engineers on real integration complexity.


Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Please note: Applications for this role will close on Wednesday, October 13th to ensure our team has enough time to give every candidate's application the care and attention it deserves.

  • Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

  • Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

  • We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

  • For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

  • Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

  • We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

  • Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

  • Intro Call (30 min): A conversation with a Talent Acquisition Partner to provide a high-level overview of Pleo and the role, confirm essential skills, and gauge initial alignment.

  • Hiring Manager Interview (45 min): A discussion with your future manager to evaluate your functional expertise, past experience, and role fit.

  • Pleo Challenge (60 min): A role-specific ""live session"" based on a scenario or business dilemma completed with key stakeholders.

Transparency is important to us

  • CV writing and content: AI can be useful for structure, but generic AI-written CVs often hide your real impact. We’re more likely to engage when you share specific outcomes (for example: “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z”) and explain the context around your decisions.

We’ll be looking for evidence that you understand finance workflows like reconciliation and month-end close, can translate those needs into clear requirements, and are comfortable collaborating with technical teams and external partners to deliver high-quality integrations.

  • Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Canvas Core team builds and maintains the foundational platform that powers Mural’s visual thinking experience. This includes the infinite canvas, key editor components, document editing behaviors, asset management, real-time collaboration, and the systems that enable fast, reliable, and intuitive interaction on the canvas.

We’re also responsible for the Mural UI, the real-time message protocol that enables seamless remote collaboration, and the developer-friendly APIs that internal teams use to build features like diagramming, workshops, presentations, integrations, and AI-enabled product capabilities.

Our mission is to ensure the Mural editor is fast, reliable, intuitive, and easy to build on.

We prioritize performance, simplicity, developer experience, and platform quality, enabling teams across the company to ship quickly and safely on top of Canvas Core.

YOUR MISSION

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll help design, build, and improve the Canvas platform so that the Mural editor remains reliable, high-performing, and intuitive for our users.

You’ll work on the systems that power real-time collaboration, shared document editing, spatial interactions, rendering and interaction performance, asset management, developer APIs, and AI-enabled product capabilities across the Mural editor.

Your role will be to reduce platform complexity, improve the quality and speed of Canvas development, and help teams ship high-quality editor experiences quickly and safely. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, Engineering, and other stakeholders to turn ambiguous product and platform problems into clear, maintainable technical solutions.

Senior Engineers at Mural lead by example through strong technical execution, thoughtful design, high-quality implementation, and collaborative problem-solving. They help raise the bar for their team through design discussions, code reviews, mentoring, documentation, and pragmatic improvements to engineering practices.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own and deliver new Canvas platform capabilities and improvements from problem definition through implementation, release, measurement, and iteration

  • Partner with Product and Design to shape high-quality user experiences, balancing pragmatic technical delivery with long-term platform needs

  • Design and build maintainable Canvas platform systems, with accountability for quality, performance, reliability, and developer experience

  • Contribute to developer-friendly APIs, service boundaries, and platform contracts that internal teams can build on quickly and safely

  • Use AI-assisted tools and agentic workflows as part of your engineering practice to prototype, implement, test, document, and measure work effectively

  • Strengthen the team through technical design reviews, demos, code reviews, mentoring, and improvements to engineering practices

  • Build and evolve canvas systems with rich document and object models, including hierarchical scene or document structures, spatial indexing and querying, layout behavior, asset management, and selection mechanics

  • Work on large-scale concurrent and real-time collaboration systems that keep shared documents synchronized across users, contributing to design decisions around event ordering, latency, conflict handling, and failure-mode management

  • Help design, build, and integrate AI-enabled product capabilities where they intersect with the canvas, document model, real-time collaboration systems, or developer platform

  • Improve performance through profiling, bottleneck analysis, architectural simplification, targeted optimization, and moving expensive work out of critical interaction paths so systems remain responsive as document complexity and user activity scale

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

  • Fluency in modern JavaScript/TypeScript, with familiarity in React, Node.js, or comparable modern frameworks

  • 6+ years building and shipping large-scale production software as part of an agile engineering team

  • Strong engineering judgment, with experience designing and delivering scalable, reliable, high-performance systems and developer-facing abstractions that balance simplicity, developer experience, and long-term maintainability

  • Experience designing clean API contracts and service boundaries, including thoughtful data models, versioning, validation, error handling, documentation, and long-term maintainability

  • Experience building distributed, concurrent, collaborative, or low-latency systems, such as collaboration tools, MMO games, shared-state systems, messaging protocols, or other low-latency user experiences, with familiarity across synchronization, consistency, event ordering, latency, failure modes, and performance trade-offs

  • Exposure to complex systems with rich object models, including hierarchical scene or document structures, spatial indexing and querying, layout behavior, asset management, selection mechanics, and performance-sensitive user interactions is a strong plus

  • Interest in AI-enabled product capabilities, or hands-on experience building or integrating them in production, such as intelligent editing, automation, recommendations, semantic document understanding, or collaboration features powered by AI

  • Performance optimization experience, including profiling, bottleneck analysis, memory and CPU efficiency, latency reduction, and responsiveness as document complexity and user activity scale

  • Familiarity with parallel processing, off-main-thread architectures, rendering pipelines, background computation, or other multithreaded systems is a plus

  • Practical experience using AI-assisted tools to prototype, implement, test, document, and measure engineering work

  • Communication and collaboration skills, with a low-ego approach to working with Product, Design, and Engineering, and the ability to contribute meaningfully to technical discussions, collaborate across teams, and help improve team engineering practices

  • Comfort operating in high-growth, fast-paced environments or scale-ups is a plus

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

About Plentific

Plentific is pioneering real-time property operations for real-world impact. Our platform connects property owners, operators, service providers and residents, and covers more than 1.7 million properties and 5,000+ service providers. We believe property repairs, maintenance and management can and should work better for everyone. That means giving landlords more control, supporting trade professionals and strengthening the communities they serve.

The Role

Inventory à l'échelle globale. Vous garantissez la fiabilité, la performance et l'harmonisation des processus, des outils et des pratiques au sein du réseau de Service Centers (SAV Robotique). Vous êtes également responsable de la disponibilité des pièces, de la maîtrise des stocks et de leur optimisation afin de soutenir les objectifs de performance opérationnelle et financière.

Missions :

Gérer les approvisionnements et les stocks à l’échelle globale

  • Superviser les flux critiques de planification et d'approvisionnement afin de garantir la disponibilité des pièces.
  • Valider les propositions d'ordres de transfert et suivre les encours critiques.

  • Être force de proposition sur les stratégies d'approvisionnement et d'optimisation des stocks.
  • Garantir la disponibilité des pièces tout en maîtrisant les coûts associés et les niveaux d'inventaire.
  • Piloter les actions de réduction des stocks dormants et obsolètes.
  • Définir les stratégies de gestion du cycle de vie des pièces et de prévention de l'obsolescence.
  • Définir les standards de performance logistique et accompagner les équipes locales dans le suivi des partenaires transport.
  • Soutenir les équipes locales dans la résolution des situations complexes.

Développer l’excellence opérationnelle Supply Chain

  • Garantir la cohérence, l'efficacité et la performance des processus Supply Chain au sein de l'ensemble des Service Centers.
  • Définir, formaliser et déployer les standards métiers en matière de Supply Chain, de gestion des stocks et de planification.
  • Animer les démarches d'amélioration continue des pratiques logistiques, d'approvisionnement et de gestion des stocks.
  • Identifier les écarts de performance, analyser leurs causes racines et piloter les plans d'actions associés.
  • Promouvoir le partage des bonnes pratiques et le retour d'expérience entre les différentes régions.

Être le référent des outils et systèmes

  • Agir en tant que Super Key User des outils Supply Chain, Inventory et Logistique (SAP, DDMRP, Power BI et outils associés).
  • Assurer le paramétrage métier, la cohérence des données de référence et le respect des standards de gestion.
  • Accompagner les utilisateurs dans l'adoption et l'utilisation optimale des outils.
  • Développer et maintenir les supports de formation ainsi que la documentation métier.
  • Contribuer à la définition de la roadmap fonctionnelle des outils en collaboration avec les équipes IT, Data et métiers.
  • Identifier les opportunités de digitalisation et d'automatisation des processus Supply Chain.

Piloter la performance Supply Chain

  • Être garant de l'atteinte des objectifs mondiaux de disponibilité des pièces, de valeur de stock, de rotation des stocks et de réduction des stocks obsolètes.
  • Animer les revues de performance Supply Chain avec les différentes régions et assurer le suivi des plans d'actions associés.
  • Définir et suivre les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) Supply Chain.
  • Faire évoluer les tableaux de bord et outils de pilotage en collaboration avec les équipes Data.
  • Analyser les tendances, identifier les risques opérationnels et les opportunités d'amélioration.
  • Proposer et piloter les actions correctives permettant d'améliorer la disponibilité des pièces, le niveau de service et la maîtrise des stocks.
  • Assurer un reporting régulier auprès du management.

  • Conduire ou contribuer aux projets structurants liés aux processus, aux outils, à la gestion des stocks et à l'organisation logistique.
  • Coordonner le déploiement de nouvelles solutions, méthodologies et évolutions systèmes.
  • Participer aux projets de transformation majeurs (ERP, hubs logistiques, optimisation des stocks, Demand Planning, digitalisation des processus, etc.).
  • Assurer l'alignement entre les besoins opérationnels des Service Centers et les objectifs stratégiques de l'entreprise.

  • Excellente maîtrise des processus Supply Chain et de gestion des stocks.
  • Bonne connaissance des principes de Demand Planning, Forecasting et Inventory Management.
  • Bonne connaissance de SAP.
  • Maîtrise avancée d'Excel, Power BI et des outils d'analyse de données (BigQuery apprécié).
  • Connaissance Solide des méthodologies Lean et d'amélioration continue appréciée.

About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Summary

Dust is hiring a Head of AI Deployment &
column2:
Partner Delivery to make high-impact Dust deployments repeatable at scale.

When customers deploy Dust well, AI agents become part of how their teams work every day. Your job is to make that happen consistently, whether a deployment is led by Dust or by a trusted partner. You will lead our most complex customer deployments, turn what works, technically and organizationally, into clear playbooks, and build the partner delivery capacity that lets more customers succeed with Dust in 2027 and beyond.

This is a player-coach leadership role. You will lead and grow Dust’s global AI Deployment team, stay directly involved in our most important deployments, and build the methods, standards, and partner network that allow delivery to scale without depending on you for every engagement.

You will work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering to connect what customers want to achieve with how deployments are planned, delivered, and measured.

This is a chance to define how an AI-native company delivers transformation: what an exceptional deployment looks like, how value is measured, and how partners become delivery teams our customers trust.

What you’ll do

Lead and grow the global AI Deployment team

  • Lead Dust’s existing global AI Deployment team and set its direction, priorities, and standards.

  • Hire and develop deployment leaders and practitioners as customer demand grows.

  • Shape roles, career paths, and coverage across regions, customer segments, and deployment types.

  • Coach the team through complex customer situations and hold a consistently high bar for the work.

  • Set up the operating rhythms, capacity planning, and reporting the function needs to scale.

Define how Dust deployments are delivered

  • Build one deployment method, from discovery through handoff, that Dust and partner teams can both follow to the same standard.

  • Define which deployments Dust should lead, which a partner can deliver well, and how work moves between the two.

  • Set clear entry and exit criteria and go-live readiness checks, and track delivery health: time to first value, go-live quality, and customer satisfaction.

  • Run regular delivery reviews, spot at-risk engagements early, and bring the right Dust and partner people together quickly when a deployment is blocked.

  • Turn lessons from each engagement into reusable playbooks, templates, and reference architectures, and recurring friction into clear input for Product and Engineering.

Lead AI transformation with strategic customers

  • Personally lead complex, high-priority, and first-of-their-kind deployments, from scoping to lasting adoption, bringing in Solutions Engineering, Product, and Engineering when complexity or risk calls for it.

  • Help customer leaders define what AI transformation means for their organization: map how teams work today and identify the workflows where agents can create the most value.

  • Align executives, IT, security, and business teams on goals, use cases, and success measures, with a baseline before launch and measured impact after.

  • Design change programs for each deployment: executive sponsorship, communication plans, role-based enablement, and clear adoption milestones.

  • Develop AI operators and champions inside customer teams, and help customers update ways of working, governance, and ownership so agents become part of how teams operate.

  • Track adoption after launch, act quickly when teams aren’t changing how they work, and hand off to Customer Success with a clear picture of what comes next.

Build a high-quality partner delivery network

  • Work with Partnerships to assess partners’ delivery capability, technical depth, and customer readiness.

  • Start with a small, carefully selected group of partner practitioners and grow capacity as quality is proven.

  • Co-create onboarding, training, certification, and train-the-trainer programs so partners can develop their own Dust experts.

  • Co-deliver early partner engagements, then help partners progress toward delivering independently, leading adoption, not just implementation.

  • Ensure customers experience Dust and its partners as one aligned team, with clear responsibilities on every engagement.

Requirements

  • You have at least 6 years of experience leading and developing customer-facing deployment or delivery teams, ideally across multiple regions or customer segments and through periods of fast change.

  • You have led complex enterprise deployments or transformation programs and delivered measurable customer outcomes.

  • You have built or significantly improved a deployment methodology, professional services model, or delivery function, adding the structure needed to scale without unnecessary process.

  • You have led organizational change alongside technology rollouts, and built champion networks or adoption plans that changed how teams work after the project ended.

    You don’t need to be a machine-learning engineer. Beyond that, we care more about evidence that you have built high-performing delivery systems than about a perfect sequence of titles.

  • You understand how systems integrators, consultancies, and implementation partners staff, deliver, and grow a practice, and you have built enablement or certification programs that created lasting capability in teams you didn’t manage.

  • You have turned around engagements at risk from scope, staffing, technical complexity, or stakeholder misalignment, and you know when to standardize, when to adapt, and when to reset.

  • You are credible with customer executives, partner leaders, and technical practitioners, and you communicate clearly with all of them.

  • You are a hands-on, low-ego leader with a builder’s instinct: you would rather solve the problem than hand off a recommendation.

  • You are comfortable traveling to customers and partners when it matters most.

AI and technical credibility

  • Advise customers on where AI agents can create meaningful value and where they can’t yet, and explain why to technical teams, business leaders, and executives.

  • Understand how agents work in practice: prompting, context, tool use, retrieval, evaluations, reliability, and cost.

  • Challenge a deployment plan’s assumptions about integrations, data connectors, authentication, permissions, security, and production readiness, and discuss the trade-offs with engineers.

  • Design evaluation approaches that connect AI performance to customer and business outcomes.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

🏨 The Company

Resilience Care, a leading player in remote medical monitoring and a partner in clinical research, is a French company founded in 2021 with a single mission: to provide better care.

Our company offers remote monitoring solutions in oncology, gastroenterology, and psychiatry, based on the collection of ePROs combined with AI technologies. These solutions rely on a monitoring platform for healthcare professionals—enabling the early detection of side effects for continuous and proactive care—and a mobile app for patients, empowering them to measure and manage their symptoms using tailored resources.

Our solutions optimize patient care, continuously enrich our understanding of patients throughout their healthcare journey, and accelerate clinical research through the collection, structuring, and in-depth analysis of real-world data. Today, our solutions are deployed in routine care for 35,000 patients across more than 200 healthcare facilities, as well as within the framework of around twenty academic and industrial clinical trials.

Through this, we put data at the service of healthcare and therapeutic innovation, driven by the ambition to enable every patient to benefit from personalized medicine.

📝 Your Role

In a few words

Within QARA, you oversee Good Clinical Practice compliance across Resilience’s sponsored studies and studies conducted with pharmaceutical partners. You combine clinical quality, data integrity and system qualification, working closely with the teams running studies and building data workflows.

Your impact

You help keep studies inspection-ready, data reliable and traceable, and compliance embedded in everyday work. Your role is to safeguard the framework and help teams apply it, rather than produce the data yourself.

Your day-to-day work

  • Oversee study GCP compliance, manage deviations and corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs), and conduct quality and Trial Master File (TMF) reviews.

  • Maintain inspection readiness and support CRO oversight in line with ICH E6(R3).

  • Qualify systems, assess test environments and review data extractions, audit trails and Data Management Plans.

  • Work with Data and Clinical teams to build compliance into data workflows from the outset.

  • Maintain clinical quality procedures, train teams and monitor regulatory developments.

This is not a site-monitoring, data-engineering, study-project-management or routine clinical data-production role.

✨ Your Team

Here, we don’t work in silos. You’ll join an agile structure where compliance is truly a team sport:

  • Your Manager: Yasmine, the guardian of regulatory compliance for our medical devices. She will share her strategic vision of the healthcare sector with you and will be your go-to for the most sensitive decisions.

  • Your core team: A trio of passionate experts. They’re your daily contacts for everything related to the quality management system, technical files, and audit preparation.

  • The team’s little extra: A unique context where safety, clinical, and regulatory aspects come together to better serve patients, led by a team that combines rigor and kindness.

You join QARA and report directly to Yasmine. You work with Clinical Operations, Clinical Scientists, Data and Translational Research, as well as the DPO, CROs and pharmaceutical partners.

👤 Candidate Profile

⚙️ You are the right person if you know how to

  • Apply ICH E6(R3), Annex 11 and 21 CFR Part 11 to clinical studies and systems.

  • Manage deviations, CAPAs, audits and inspection preparation, beyond data cleaning alone.

  • Qualify systems using CSV/CSQ approaches and apply ALCOA+ principles.

  • Work with EDC systems and ePRO/eCOA solutions, translating their requirements into practical controls.

  • Communicate and write fluently in English.

🙂 You are the right person if you have

  • A rigorous approach that takes operational constraints into account.

  • Practical judgement to turn requirements into workable processes.

  • The ability to influence and train colleagues rather than impose rules.

  • Confidence working across clinical and technical teams and with external partners.

📃 You are the right person if you have already

  • Gained at least five years of relevant experience in Clinical Data Management and GCP compliance within a pharmaceutical company or CRO.

  • Handled clinical quality topics such as deviations, audits, inspections or procedures.

  • Contributed to computerised system qualification.

  • Worked with EDC systems, such as Medidata Rave, Veeva or Oracle, and ePRO/eCOA solutions.

It’s a plus if you

  • Understand pipelines, ETL and databases, without needing to be a developer.

  • Know CDISC standards for regulatory submissions.

  • Want to move from data production to compliance oversight and help build quality practices.

💛 Why join us?

  • Contribute to reliable studies and data that support clinical research in oncology.

  • Combine clinical quality, data integrity and collaboration with technical teams.

  • Work remotely from France and meet colleagues at internal company events.

  2. Interview with Yasmine, your future manager.

  3. Case study with Sarah and Yasmine from QARA.

  4. Team conversation with Nicoleta, Bertille and Alric.

About Stableton

Stableton is a globally leading, tech- and data-driven institutional investor in private blue-chip tech companies. We empower institutional investors, private banks, and wealth managers to benefit from the value creation of the world's most valuable technology companies through our unique unicorn index investment funds and institutional thematic investment mandates.

With our disruptive mindset, fast-paced culture, and track record of innovation, we are reshaping private market investing. With seven years of 100%+ annual growth, we are scaling globally, and we're just getting started.

Your Role

This is a part-time role supporting our fund operations and structuring teams. You will take on the recurring documentation and data work that keeps our fund records complete and audit-ready: gathering account statements, logging them into our database, and working through structured clean-up tasks.

We are a tech-enabled firm and we expect you to work that way. Using AI tools to speed up repetitive work is not a bonus here, it is part of how the role is done.

This is not an internship. It takes time to learn how our funds and structures work and where accuracy matters, so we are looking for someone who wants to stay in the role and grow with it.

Your Responsibilities

  • Gather account statements and log them into our database
  • Work through structured clean-up tasks to bring fund records to a consistent standard
  • Support the team with recurring documentation and filing work
  • Take on ad hoc requests across fund operations and structuring as they come up

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree completed, currently enrolled in a Master's program in finance, economics, law, or a related field
  • Previous experience in audit, banking, or financial services. This is a must, not a nice to have
  • Available at least 50% alongside your studies. Hours are flexible so you can keep your studies on track
  • Ready to commit for at least six months
  • Strong Excel skills and comfort working with structured data
  • Fluent with AI tools and quick to figure out where they save time
  • Precise and reliable. You care whether a record is correct, not just complete
  • Comfortable working independently and asking when something is unclear
  • Fluent in English
column2:

Benefits

  • Real ownership of the documentation and data groundwork, not shadowing
  • A team that actually uses AI tools in daily work, and room to bring your own
  • Insight into how funds are operated and structured at a regulated Swiss asset manager
  • Close collaboration with a small, senior team
  • Flexible hours around your study schedule and a hybrid setup in Zurich
  • A role you can grow into over at least six months
  • If it works well on both sides, we'd be glad to keep you on full-time after you graduate

Stableton is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Proteins are the molecular machines of life, used for many therapeutic, diagnostic, chemical, agricultural and food applications. Designing and optimizing proteins takes a lot of expert knowledge and manual effort, through the use of custom computational and biological tools.

Machine learning is revolutionizing this space, by enabling high-fidelity protein models. At Cradle, we offer a software platform for AI-guided discovery and optimization of proteins, so that biologists can design proteins faster and at scale. We are already used by clients across biopharma, biotech, agri-tech, food-tech, and academia.

We're an experienced team of just under 100 people. We've built many successful products before and have enough funding for multiple years of runway. We are distributed across three offices in Amsterdam, Boston, and Zurich, alongside a few remote colleagues.

We offer our employees a very competitive salary, a generous equity stake in the company and a wide range of benefits and career progression opportunities.

The Role

As Executive Assistant at Cradle, you'll keep two of our founding executives moving. Between customer visits, investor meetings, hiring and travel across Amsterdam, Zurich and the US, there's a lot to keep track of, and your job is to make sure nothing gets dropped. You'll own their calendars, inboxes and travel, and take care of the personal admin that would otherwise eat into their time.   • Take care of personal and life admin: Appointments, household logistics, official paperwork, bills and renewals, handled so none of it lands on their desks.

We are The Robotics Company, building the infrastructure that enables robots to be deployed at scale.

In just six months, we’ve grown from $0 to $1M in revenue, driven by strong demand for what we’re building. Our mission is to build the foundational infrastructure that brings intelligent robots out of the lab and into the real world.

About the Internship

We’re looking for exceptional students who are excited to work at the intersection of robotics, AI, and real-world deployment.

As an Engineering Intern, you’ll work directly alongside our research and engineering teams on meaningful technical problems, contribute to systems running on real robots, and gain hands-on experience building at an early-stage robotics company.

  • Work alongside our researchers and engineers to develop and test robotics and AI systems.

  • Contribute to projects across robot learning, perception, manipulation, navigation, simulation, or robotics infrastructure.

  • Prototype, implement, and evaluate new algorithms and technical approaches.

  • Test software and models in simulation and on real robotic systems.

  • Take ownership of a meaningful technical project with direct mentorship from the team.

What We Look For

  • Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, AI/ML, Computer Vision, Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++.

  • Hands-on experience through robotics projects, research labs, internships, competitions, or open-source work.

  • We especially love candidates with experience in leading robotics and research labs, including SLAM, RAI, Boston Dynamics, and similar environments.

  • Familiarity with PyTorch, JAX, ROS/ROS2, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, or similar frameworks is a plus.

  • Strong technical curiosity and excitement about solving difficult problems in robotics.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving, highly collaborative environment.

We care more about what you’ve built, explored, and learned than checking every box.

If you’re excited about building intelligent robotic systems that operate in the real world, we’d love to hear from you.

About Sereact

Sereact is a Series B embodied-AI company. Cortex, our VLA model, is deployed in live warehouse robotic cells across the EU and US. Zurich is our newest research hub, focused on the manipulation and control problems that sit underneath Cortex.

The role

This is a Research Engineer position. It is scoped to the data generation layer of the VLA stack: teleoperation hardware and software, retargeting pipelines that map human demonstrations onto robot hands, and the data collection infrastructure that feeds Cortex.   • Design and maintain scalable, UMI-style data collection hardware and software that other engineers at Sereact rely on

  • Benchmark control and retargeting approaches using rigorous, human-factors-informed methodology

  • Instrument and support the physical robots deployed in the Zurich hub, including day-to-day work on the control stack

  • Work with the model-training team to define what data they need and close the loop on data quality

  • Build tooling or infrastructure outside your immediate brief when it unblocks the wider team

  • Working knowledge of retargeting algorithms for mapping human input onto robot hands or end-effectors

About the role:

ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.


You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

  • Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

  • Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

  • Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

  • Feed the product. Custom agents you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

  • Hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.

What You Will Bring to the Role

  • Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.

  • Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.

  • Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.

  • Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.

  • Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance

  • Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.

  • Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.

US Marketing Lead

Location: United States

Reports to: VP of Marketing

Employment type: Full-time

About Teton

Teton is building the autonomous operating system for care. Our technology gives senior living and care teams greater visibility into resident wellbeing, movement, sleep, and care delivery, helping them respond faster, work more efficiently, and provide more personalized care.

We are growing quickly across the United States and are looking for a US Marketing Lead to own our regional marketing strategy and execution.

The Role

The US Marketing Lead will be the territory owner for Teton’s growth and brand presence in the United States.

You will translate Teton’s global positioning and company priorities into a focused US marketing plan that creates demand, strengthens our reputation, and helps the sales team win. This is a hands-on role for someone who can set the regional strategy, build campaigns, produce sales materials, support events, coordinate PR, and measure what is working.

You will work closely with US Sales, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Events, Growth, and external partners. You will report to the VP of Marketing and serve as the primary marketing partner for the US commercial team.

What You’ll Own

US Marketing Strategy

  • Develop and execute the US marketing plan in alignment with company revenue goals and global marketing priorities.

  • Identify the audiences, markets, partnerships, and channels most likely to drive growth.

  • Adapt Teton’s global campaigns and positioning for the US senior living and care market.

  • Maintain a clear regional campaign calendar, budget, and set of priorities.

  • Bring insights from customers, prospects, competitors, and the market back into the broader marketing organization.

Demand Generation and Campaigns

  • Partner with Growth Lead to build and run integrated campaigns across email, paid media, content, webinars, events, partnerships, and other relevant channels.

  • Create campaigns around Teton’s most important customer problems and product capabilities.

  • Own regional email strategy, segmentation, nurture programs, and campaign follow-up.

  • Work with Growth to improve lead generation, conversion, and account engagement.

  • Develop targeted programs for priority accounts, operator groups, and strategic market segments.

  • Ensure leads are properly captured, routed, followed up on, and measured in HubSpot.

Sales Enablement

  • Serve as the primary marketing partner to the US sales organization.

  • Develop and maintain US-specific sales decks, case studies, one-pagers, proposals, follow-up materials, and campaign assets.

  • Translate product capabilities into clear operational and commercial value for senior living operators.

  • Equip sales with the proof points, customer stories, and market insights needed to move opportunities forward.

  • Support account-based campaigns for strategic prospects and active opportunities.

  • Gather regular feedback from Sales and Customer Success to identify gaps in messaging, content, and enablement.

Events, Webinars, and Partnerships

  • Partner with the Events lead to determine which US conferences, webinars, executive gatherings, and field programs deserve investment.

  • Build pre-event, on-site, and post-event campaigns that generate meetings and measurable pipeline.

  • Support speaker submissions, presentations, sponsorships, customer participation, and event messaging.

  • Develop regional partnerships with associations, media organizations, technology partners, and other industry stakeholders.

  • Ensure events are connected to broader campaigns rather than treated as standalone activities.

Content, Customer Stories, and PR

  • Identify strong US customer stories and work with Customer Success to turn them into case studies, testimonials, videos, and campaign assets.

  • Develop content that reflects the priorities and language of US senior living operators.

  • Work with internal subject-matter experts to produce thought leadership, educational content, reports, and webinars.

  • Coordinate with Teton’s PR partners on announcements, contributed articles, awards, speaking opportunities, and media relationships.

  • Help establish Teton and its leadership as credible voices in the US senior living market.

Product Positioning and Market Intelligence

  • Localize global product positioning for US audiences while maintaining consistency with Teton’s overall narrative.

  • Develop messaging for different US customer segments, buyer roles, and stages of the sales process.

  • Monitor competitors, category trends, customer needs, and changes in the senior living market.

  • Partner with Product Marketing and Product to support launches and communicate new capabilities effectively.

  • Ensure US market feedback is reflected in future campaigns, content, and product messaging.

Measurement and Reporting

  • Define regional goals and report on campaign performance, lead generation, pipeline contribution, event results, and channel effectiveness.

  • Maintain clear dashboards and regular updates for Marketing and US commercial leadership.

  • Use performance data to improve targeting, messaging, campaign investment, and sales follow-up.

  • Establish a consistent process for evaluating what is working, what is not, and where the team should focus next.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

  • Established a clear and credible US marketing strategy tied to Teton’s commercial goals.

  • Built a consistent campaign engine that generates qualified demand and supports pipeline growth.

  • Improved the quality and consistency of US sales enablement.

  • Created a repeatable approach to US events, webinars, partnerships, and account-based programs.

  • Expanded Teton’s library of US customer proof points and case studies.

  • Increased Teton’s visibility and credibility with senior living operators and industry stakeholders.

  • Created transparent reporting that shows how US marketing contributes to revenue.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of B2B marketing experience, ideally in healthcare technology, senior living, or enterprise software industry.

  • Experience owning a regional, vertical, or business-unit marketing strategy.

  • A track record of building integrated campaigns that contribute to pipeline and revenue.

  • Strong sales enablement experience and the ability to work closely with enterprise sales teams.

  • Experience with events, content, email marketing, webinars, account-based marketing, and demand generation.

  • Excellent writing, editing, messaging, and presentation skills.

  • Strong project-management skills and the ability to move between strategy and hands-on execution.

  • Comfort working in a fast-growing company where priorities can change and processes are still being built.

  • Strong analytical judgment and experience using marketing and CRM data to make decisions.

  • Familiarity with HubSpot, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, and related marketing tools is preferred.

  • Knowledge of the US senior living or healthcare market is highly valuable.

The Person We Think Will Thrive

You are a strong generalist who knows how to turn company goals into focused regional execution. You can write a campaign brief, improve a sales deck, develop an event plan, interview a customer, analyze lead performance, and present a clear recommendation to leadership.

You are commercially minded, comfortable working directly with sales, and focused on producing work that helps the company grow. You bring structure without creating unnecessary process, and you know how to balance brand building with near-term pipeline needs.

Unleash AI Innovators, Securely

Software is being rewritten in real time. AI agents are starting to write more code than humans do, at a speed no security team has ever had to match, and that single shift is opening up the biggest opportunity our industry has seen in a decade. We're not bracing for it, we're building the company that owns it.

Snyk is building the next generation security platform where security isn't a set of tools people operate. These agents work alongside both the company build and the agents they adopt. Security stops being a queue of work waiting for people, and becomes a coordinated workforce companies direct and trust.

Description
column11: >Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes.
column21:

column53: >Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution.
column72: >Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy.
column91: >Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters.
column110: >Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo.
column142: >Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer.

Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first ""wow"" moment themselves. When they say ""that won't work for us"" or ""we'll build it ourselves"", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not ""lawyer who is good with computers"". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why ""they did not understand the value"" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
  • We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
  • Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
  • Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
  • Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.

Your Role

We ship fast, and we intend to keep shipping fast. The consequence is that our system is outgrowing the amount of deliberate design that went into it. We run AI agents over customer documents in a domain where being wrong is expensive, and a lot of the load-bearing decisions about how those fit together are still implicit.

You will be making those decisions explicit and then making them hold. That means codifying golden paths, building the shared primitives and APIs that product engineers work on top of, owning the architecture of the system as a whole, and establishing what our reliability actually needs to be before an incident establishes it for us.

Platform at Cortea sits between software engineering, DevOps and SRE. Its customers are other engineers. This is not a DevOps role under a different name: you will spend more time in application code than in YAML, and the reason we want infrastructure experience is that we don't believe you can design a system well without being able to run it.

The bar we are hiring against is someone who has taken a system from nothing to production and owned it end to end. You picked the technology, argued the tradeoffs in writing, provisioned the infrastructure, and were responsible for it when it broke.


On AI

We use AI heavily and we want you to. What we are not looking for is someone who outsources their judgment to it.

The mental model of this system has to live in your head, not in a context window. Use agents to move quickly on implementation. Do the design, the reasoning and the writing yourself, and be able to defend every decision you ship.


What you'll do

Four areas, roughly in the order you will spend time on them. You won't work on all of them at once, but you should be open to any of them.

Product platform. Make the easiest way for product engineers to do something (the paved road, or golden path) also the most secure, reliable and scalable way by default. Build the shared primitives, libraries and APIs that hide complexity and carry our quality and observability standards with them. Own the architecture and the core stack: what gets standardized, what gets reused, and where the system should be in eighteen months.

Infrastructure, observability and reliability. Infrastructure as code by default, from cloud resources through to dashboards and alerts. Provision, run and tune our Kubernetes cluster and cloud footprint, and keep CI fast as the deploy rate grows. Define SLIs for the workloads that
matter, build SLOs on top of them, and make the alerting high-signal enough that people trust it. Drive down AI and infrastructure spend.

Security and compliance. Keep the internal foundations secure by default: IAM, dependency management, secrets. Own the authentication and authorization stack, including ReBAC models covering both humans and agents. Implement SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls without taxing every future change.

AI dev tooling. Keep product engineers and their agents on the paved road by making sure the documentation and agent guidelines they need are in place. Shorten the path from design to implementation with standardized automations and development environments that stay close to production.


What this looks like in practice

  • A system of record for managing and distributing constantly evolving agent configurations, under strict auditability and tenant isolation requirements

  • The harnesses powering our AI agents, abstracting over use cases that change faster than the code

  • Centralized progress tracking that holds up across a growing number of parallel agent executions

  • Usage-based tenant billing with quotas and rate limiting across a growing set of products

  • SLIs for the background job system behind our agents (execution latency, AI spend, memory, CPU), then fixing the bottlenecks they expose at both the application and infrastructure level

  • A document pipeline handling dozens of file formats, very large spreadsheets and hundreds of parallel uploads, under a strong reliability requirement


You will fit into this role if you…

  • Have designed, built and operated distributed systems end to end, and enjoy understanding how every part interacts with the rest

  • Are strong at backend software engineering and at DevOps/SRE, and don't think of those as separate jobs

  • Write design docs, RFCs, ADRs, postmortems

  • Reach for simple, boring solutions first, can tell essential complexity from accidental, and know which corners are safe to cut and which ones compound

  • Can turn a hard problem on its head and find the alternative nobody proposed

Concretely, you have scaled Postgres or another relational transactional database under real load, run production Kubernetes, and built observability rather than inherited it: SLIs, SLOs, distributed tracing.

No one checks every box. If you have designed a system from scratch, run it in production, and can explain in writing why it is shaped the way it is, let's talk.


Nice-to-haves that are a plus:

  • Durable workflow orchestrators like Temporal, and background job and queue processing generally

  • Infrastructure for LLM-based products or agentic systems

  • Audit, finance, compliance, or another high-accuracy domain

  • Azure and/or GCP


This is probably not the right role if…

  • You would describe application code as someone else's responsibility. A large share of platform work here happens inside the product codebase.

  • Your answer to reliability is more process. We want guardrails, not gates.

  • You need a well-defined system to work in. Ours is not one yet, and shaping it is the job.


What you will get

  • Real influence on strategy. In a small team of excellent engineers and operators with high autonomy, you will shape product direction. Best idea wins, regardless of seniority.

  • Meaningful equity and competitive salary. You are one of the first to build this, and you share in the upside.

  • A mission that matters. Building intelligent systems for a $200bn industry. From Berlin, with AI at the core.

  • Second Call — Technical interview with Dan

    ElevenLabs is looking for a Value Strategist to help our customers identify, quantify, and realize the business value of ElevenLabs across our portfolio, with a primary focus on ElevenAgents.

    This is a senior individual contributor role within our global Revenue organization, spanning the full customer lifecycle from early sales conversations through proof of concept, deployment, renewal, and expansion. You will work directly with customers and prospects to understand their businesses, build the case for investment, and establish how that value will be measured over time.

    On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

    This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

    You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

    In this role you will

    • Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

    • Build our global value strategy. Develop the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, discovery approaches, and playbooks that define how ElevenLabs approaches value across industries and use cases.

    • Scale what works. Turn bespoke work with our largest customers into repeatable approaches that enable our Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial teams to articulate and measure value without requiring bespoke support for every customer.

    • Identify where ElevenLabs can have the greatest impact. Develop a deep understanding of a customer's business, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities to determine which use cases have the greatest potential and why.

    • Quantify the opportunity. Build rigorous financial and operational models that translate ElevenLabs use cases into measurable outcomes across revenue, cost, productivity, customer experience, and other relevant dimensions.

    • Define how value will be proven. Establish success metrics and measurement approaches for proofs of concept and deployments so that customers and ElevenLabs have a shared understanding of what success looks like from the outset.

    • Measure value realization. Partner with customers and internal teams after deployment to understand the impact ElevenLabs is delivering, identify gaps between expected and realized value, and determine where additional opportunities exist.

    • Support expansion and long-term customer value. Use insights from existing deployments to help customers understand what they have achieved and identify where ElevenLabs can drive additional impact.

    • Work directly with the data. Analyze customer and industry data, build models, pressure-test assumptions, and develop recommendations yourself. You should be equally comfortable working in the details and communicating the implications.

    • Partner with Deployment. On strategic accounts, work alongside Deployment Strategists who own the account-level business case, contributing methodology and capturing what works into reusable assets. Across the rest of the book, be the primary owner of value quantification and measurement.

    • Influence senior stakeholders. Communicate complex analysis simply and credibly, and engage with senior leaders internally and externally when the opportunity requires it.

    Requirements

    • 10+ years of relevant experience across operating roles, strategy, management consulting, analytics, finance, customer strategy, or other roles requiring rigorous business problem solving.

    • Strong operating judgment. You understand how businesses work and can quickly get underneath a customer's operating model, workflows, economics, and strategic priorities.

    • Exceptional analytical ability. You can personally build sophisticated financial and operational models, work with incomplete or imperfect information, make assumptions explicit, and turn analysis into decisions.

    • Structured problem solving. You are comfortable starting with an ambiguous question such as ""Where could AI create the most value in this business?"" and developing a rigorous approach to answering it.

    • Customer credibility. You can work directly with customers across functions and levels, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and establish trust quickly.

    • Commercial judgment. You understand how business value connects to technology investment decisions and can partner closely with Revenue teams while maintaining an objective, customer-first perspective.

    • Excellent communication. You can distill complex analysis into a clear point of view and communicate it effectively in writing and verbally, from working teams through senior executives.

    • A builder mentality. You are excited to start by doing the work yourself, learn from customers, and turn what works into scalable methodologies and tools.

    • Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You can move quickly across industries, customer types, and use cases while maintaining a high bar for analytical rigor.

    • Ability to operate globally. You are comfortable partnering with teams and customers across regions and traveling when valuable for customer work.

    • Willingness to travel. Must be willing and able to travel up to 10% of the time.

    • Experience in strategy or management consulting, particularly in operational transformation, technology, customer experience, or growth.

    • Experience as an operator within a technology company or other fast-moving business.

    • Experience working on AI, automation, customer experience, or technology-enabled business transformation.

    • Experience developing business cases, value frameworks, or analytical methodologies that were ultimately scaled beyond an individual project or customer.

>Join GlassDollar and help build the system some of Europe's largest companies use to find, test, and adopt startup technology.
We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than ""implement what's in the ticket"". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked.
We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them.
column5:
>Large organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting.
GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow.
Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems.



What we're looking for

You can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like ""customers need a better way to manage X"". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here.

You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions.

You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached.

You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them.

You can work across the stack. A feature might run from a React interaction through GraphQL into a Node service, a schema redesign, a permissions update, and a safe migration for existing customers. Curiosity to follow the problem matters more than equal depth everywhere.

You own quality. We have QA. That's not where quality begins. What breaks if this request happens twice? What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence.

You communicate like your decisions will matter later. Six months from now, somebody should understand an important decision without digging through seventeen Slack messages and a deleted Notion comment. That means writing things down when they matter, explaining trade-offs clearly, giving useful code reviews, and surfacing risks before they become incidents.

You raise the engineering bar around you. You do not need a management title to have influence. Find the hole in an architecture, unblock someone without taking the keyboard away, disagree without turning every decision into a referendum. As you earn trust, you’ll naturally become the person people bring harder problems to.



What you'll do

  • Can independently take a feature from unclear starting point to production

How we hire
column33:
>We're a small engineering team, so there are fewer places for responsibility to disappear and no chain of five people between you and a decision. We prefer written context over meetings the calendar invented, and working software over elaborate process.
Quickly doesn't mean carelessly. Sometimes the fastest route is the simple version today, sometimes it's another day on a foundation twenty future features will sit on. Knowing which situation you're in is part of the job. Expect to ship to production very early.

>How we hireNo seven-stage endurance test. No algorithm trivia disconnected from the work.
  1. Intro. You, us, and whether this is the environment you're actually looking for.
  2. Technical conversation. We go deep on something difficult you've built: the decisions, the alternatives, what you'd do differently now.
  3. Technical assessment. Usually live coding on a realistic problem, sometimes a small proof of concept instead. We care how you think, not whether your solution matches ours.
  4. Offer. If there's strong mutual conviction, we move.
